lead: Seven publications this week. Biology had three, on conservation agreements, invasive bass removal in Gatineau Park, and permit spawning in the Florida Keys. Health Sciences had two, on corticosteroid treatment for Duchenne muscular dystrophy and on care for Inuit travelling from the Qikiqtani region to Ottawa. Neuroscience had one on maternal stress and infant development, and Physics had one ATLAS search with six Carleton authors. The records show no collaborations between Carleton units this week, and the ATLAS paper is the only large-collaboration work.

items.title: The enduring benefits of temporary conservation agreements
items.summary: The title indicates a paper in Biological Conservation on the lasting benefits of temporary conservation agreements. No abstract was available, so the methods and findings cannot be described here.

items.title: A case study on attempts to remove invasive Largemouth Bass from two small lakes in Québec
items.venue: North American Journal of Fisheries Management
items.summary: Researchers and community partners spent three years removing invasive Largemouth Bass from two small lakes in Gatineau Park, using nest destruction, angling, seining and traps. Active nests in Lac Kingsmere fell from 25 to 0 and catches dropped by over 90% in abundance, but eradication would need several more years of monitoring, and community participation was important for early detection and sustained effort.

items.title: Spawning site residency and connectivity patterns of permit (Trachinotus falcatus) in response to a seasonal fishing closure in the Florida Keys
items.summary: The title indicates a study of how permit (a sport fish) stay at and move between spawning sites in the Florida Keys in response to a seasonal fishing closure. No abstract was available, so the methods and findings cannot be described here.

items.title: Muscle function, linear growth, and bone health during 30 months of vamorolone, prednisone, and deflazacort treatment for Duchenne muscular dystrophy: a comparative study
items.venue: Journal of Bone and Mineral Research
items.summary: This study compared 30 months of vamorolone treatment in boys with Duchenne muscular dystrophy against matched boys on prednisone or deflazacort, the standard corticosteroids, using data from separate non-randomized trials. Motor function did not differ significantly between the drugs, but height stayed stable on vamorolone and fell on the other two, and vertebral fractures were about half as frequent.

items.title: Timing matters: Maternal stress and mental health symptoms from pregnancy to postpartum in shaping infant development
items.summary: The study followed 146 Pakistani mother-infant pairs from pregnancy to postpartum and linked maternal stress, depressive symptoms and a physiological stress measure to poorer infant fine motor skills. Higher social support after birth weakened the link between prenatal stress and fine motor skills, which suggests that support and lower postpartum stress could help, though the findings are associations.

items.title: Search for dark photons from Higgs boson decays in the gluon-gluon fusion channel in proton-proton collisions at $$ \sqrt{s}=13.6 $$ TeV with the ATLAS detector
items.summary: The ATLAS collaboration searched 135 fb-1 of 2023 and 2024 collision data for Higgs bosons decaying into a photon and a dark photon, using a trigger with lower energy thresholds introduced in 2023. No significant excess over Standard Model predictions was found, so the result sets an upper limit of 1.4% on how often this decay occurs, tightened to 0.9% when combined with earlier Run 2 searches.
